name: Matthew J. Payne
position: Director of the Minor Planet Center
institution: Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian
address: 60 Garden Street, MS 16, Cambridge, MA 02138, USA
summary: I am an astrophysicist with research interests in the observations and dynamics of exoplanets and Solar System bodies. I am interested in the development of algorithms and open-source software for the efficient processing of large astronomical data sets, and I am enthused by the cross-disciplinary work of the planetary defense community.
specializations: Formation and evolution of small-body populations

appointments.title: Director, Minor Planet Center
details: I lead a team of 12 astronomers and software developers at the Minor Planet Center (MPC), the single worldwide location for the receipt and distribution of positional measurements of minor planets, comets and outer irregular natural satellites of the major planets, and for the identification, designation and orbit computation of all of these objects.

I lead the design and delivery of advanced tools for processing and cataloguing near-Earth objects, asteroids, comets and the natural satellites of the major planets, and manage the collection and analysis of data from a worldwide network of observatories.
I write grant proposals to fund both new research and the expansion of the MPC’s activities, and I carry out research on the observations and dynamics of Solar System bodies.
